### BCF-002 IGameClock / RunTime — Logic
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/game-clock/game_clock_run_time_test.cs` (helper: `tests/helpers/FakeGameClock.cs`)
**What to test**:
- AC-1: `IGameClock` has exactly four read-only float props `Time`, `UnscaledTime`, `DeltaTime`, `RunTime`; no setters (reflection)
- AC-2: RunTime == 0 before `MarkRunOrigin()`; == 2.0 (+/-1e-5) after origin + `Advance(2.0f)`
- AC-3: pause compensation — origin, `Advance(10f)`; `BeginPause`/`TimeScale=0`/`Advance(5f)`/`EndPause`/`TimeScale=1`/`Advance(1f)`: RunTime == 10 throughout pause, == 11 after; sampled sequence non-decreasing
- AC-4: during pause `UnscaledTime` += 0.5, `DeltaTime == 0`, `Time` unchanged; `TimeScale=1` -> `DeltaTime == dt`
- AC-5: control members (origin/pause/convert) only on the separate control interface (reflection)
- AC-6: re-marking origin resets RunTime to 0 and clears accumulator (30 s run + 5 s pause -> `Advance(1f)` == 1.0)
- AC-7: realtime-basis stamp conversion == current RunTime (3.0 after 4 s incl. 1 s pause)
- AC-8: scripted sequence (incl. `Advance(0.501f)`) run 10x on fresh clocks -> bit-identical outputs
- AC-9: not automated here (gate lands in BCF-006, not in sprint) — code review
**Edge cases to cover**: read right after `MarkRunOrigin()` == exactly 0; two consecutive pauses (5 s + 3 s) accumulate to 8 s; zero-length pause no-op; `BeginPause` while paused / `EndPause` while not paused are no-ops; `MarkRunOrigin()` while paused starts un-paused; stamp before origin -> 0 (not negative); stamp inside ended pause -> finite, 0 <= value <= RunTime, no NaN; `Advance(0f)` changes nothing
**Estimated test count**: ~16 unit tests

### BCF-004 `[DESIGNER-ERROR]` channel — Logic
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/designer-error/designer_error_channel_test.cs` (helper: `tests/helpers/RecordingDesignerErrorLog.cs`)
**What to test**:
- AC-1: `Messages[0]` starts with exact ordinal `[DESIGNER-ERROR]`
- AC-2: `Report` never throws, caller continues (Unity-backed sink with `LogAssert.Expect`, and recording sink)
- AC-3: `Count == 1`, message contains marker + system tag (`DamageHealth`); `Reset()` -> `Count == 0`
- AC-4: consumer stub that does not report -> `Count == 0`
- AC-5: Unity-backed sink matched by `LogAssert.Expect(LogType.Error, ^\[DESIGNER-ERROR\])`; without the Expect the same report fails the test
- AC-6: two sinks into two consumers; only first reports -> counts 1 and 0 (no shared state)
**Edge cases to cover**: empty message and null message still prefixed, no exception; 100 consecutive reports -> count 100; empty log after construction
**Estimated test count**: ~11 unit tests

### OP-001 Pool core — Logic
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/object-pool/object_pool_core_test.cs`
**What to test**:
- AC-1: pre-warm creates exactly config-driven counts per type, all `activeSelf == false`, parented under pool container
- AC-2: exactly one `[DESIGNER-ERROR]` when infantry total = `max_enemy_count - 1`, and when an elite/boss type count is 0
- AC-3: `Spawn` returns a member of the pre-warmed set for that type, active, at `position`, free count -1; never `Instantiate`
- AC-4: `ReturnToPool` -> inactive, free count restored; next `Spawn` (count-1 pool) returns the same reference
- AC-5: infantry exhaustion -> `null`, no exception, no designer error, pooled count unchanged; succeeds after one return
- AC-6: elite/boss exhaustion -> `null` + exactly one `[DESIGNER-ERROR]`, count unchanged
- AC-7: `ReturnToPool` raises no death/XP-shaped callback
**Edge cases to cover**: type with count 0 does not throw; changing fixture count changes instance count (nothing hardcoded); infantry total == `max_enemy_count` logs no error; every elite/boss at 1 logs none; spawning type A never yields type B; out-of-order returns restore full free count; boss behaves like elite
**Estimated test count**: ~14 unit tests

### IM-002 Parry ring buffer — Logic
**Test file path**: `tests/unit/input-manager/input_manager_parry_buffer_test.cs`
**What to test**:
- AC-1 (AC-IM-01): press at 1.000, window 120 ms: live at 1.100, not live at 1.121, count 0 after prune
- AC-2: inclusive boundary live at 1.120
- AC-3: capacity 4 + 5th press overwrites oldest -> `{1.01,1.02,1.03,1.04}`
- AC-4: `Prune(1.150)` removes 1.000 (consumed), keeps 1.100 unconsumed
- AC-5: 10x `HasLiveParryPress` non-consuming

**Edge cases to cover**: query at 1.121 without prune still false; boundary at (0.0, 0.120) and (1199.000, 1199.120) to prove no float drift (single-precision trap: `1.12f-1.0f > 0.12f`); capacity 2; overwriting a consumed press; empty-buffer prune; consumed-only buffer peeks false
**Estimated test count**: ~12 unit tests

**Test file path**: `tests/unit/input-manager/input_manager_parry_consume_test.cs`

## Manual QA Checklist

### BCF-001 Day-0 project setup — Config/Data
**Verification method**: Manual step-through, results written to `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` (config smoke)
**Who must sign off**: user (qa-lead checklist review); unity-specialist for AC-2/AC-5
**Evidence to capture**: smoke doc recording exact editor version (`6000.3.x`) and exact `com.unity.inputsystem` version; link to green CI run

Checklist:

## Smoke Test Scope

Adapted for Sprint 1: there is no main menu, new-game flow, or save system yet. `tests/smoke/critical-paths.md` (full-MVP list) is mostly N/A this sprint and should be updated at sprint close (that file is outside this plan's write scope).

Critical paths to verify before any QA hand-off for this sprint (run via `/smoke-check sprint`):

1. **Project opens and compiles clean** — Unity 6.3 LTS project opens with zero Console errors; no compile errors anywhere under `src/` or `tests/` (replaces "game launches to main menu")
2. **EditMode suite green in CI** (and locally); PlayMode step green once OP-003/BCF-005 PlayMode tests exist. No test skipped or disabled to get green
3. **Prototype player build launches and runs a 200-enemy spawn without crash** — player build (not Editor); sustained run length proposed at 5 minutes (matches critical-paths item 14 "5 minutes"); replaces "new session can be started" and the primary-mechanic check
4. **RunTime monotonic across a simulated pause** — BCF-002 AC-3 passes (RunTime does not advance or decrease across `timeScale = 0`); regression risk for parry matching
5. **Zero Instantiate after pool pre-warm** — verified in-sprint by OP-001 AC-3 (`Spawn` never instantiates) plus churn through spawn/return in OP-001/OP-002 tests; Profiler-verified player-build check is OP-006 (not in sprint) — see gap G-11. Note the prototype is isolated from `src/` and so does not exercise `ObjectPool`
6. **Performance recorded, not gated** — 50/100/200 frame-time numbers captured in PROTO-2 as a baseline; no budget gate fails the build this sprint
7. **Save / load cycle: N/A** — no persistence in MVP (architecture.md; gate-check 2026-10-10)

*N/A this sprint from `tests/smoke/critical-paths.md`: items 1-3 (selection screen), 7 (Dodge), 8 (level-up), 9-11 (elite/boss/death/win), 12 (GameDataValidator not in sprint), 14 (memory growth, covered only informally by item 3 above).*

*Smoke tests are verified by the developer via `/smoke-check`. A failed smoke check means the build is not ready for QA hand-off.*

## Playtest Requirements

| Story | Playtest Goal | Min Sessions | Target Player Type |
|-------|--------------|--------------|-------------------|
| PROTO-2 | **Balance 1 — Finisher vs Levy:** a base Finisher (starting value must be >= Levy HP 30; GDD base is 25) kills a Levy and feels like "the best moment in a standard wave" (creative-director sign-off criterion) | >=1 developer session + 2-3 external | Mix: developer + new players |
| PROTO-2 | **Balance 2 — Parry burst ceiling vs Finisher:** parry burst ceiling 80 vs Finisher 25-40: do most players parry rather than skip it, and does parry dominate the Finisher (Pillar 2)? | same sessions | experienced preferred for ceiling |
| PROTO-2 | **Balance 3 — C5 aggregate heal:** does C5 sustain / aggregate heal (OQ-11) trivialise damage? (only if the prototype includes a heal toggle; otherwise record as not-testable and carry to Sprint 2) | same sessions | experienced |
| PROTO-2 | **Balance 4 — Power vs density scaling:** with no automatic player-power scaling, does rising density outpace the player? Can a Combo-lane and a Parry-lane build both reach the 10-minute mark (M1 exit criterion; prototype proxy only, since upgrades are not in the prototype) | same sessions | experienced |
| PROTO-2 | **Feel Q1:** is combo-reset-on-damage fair (reset only at >= `reset_damage_threshold` 3 effective damage)? | same | new + experienced |
| PROTO-2 | **Feel Q2:** does combo + parry read as depth or overwhelm? | same | new players weighted |
| PROTO-2 | **Feel Q3:** momentum reset on hit: full vs half (A/B in the prototype) | same | experienced |
| PROTO-2 | **Feel Q4:** how many enemies on screen before readability breaks (50/100/200) | same | new + experienced |
| PROTO-2 | **Telegraph readability (AC-13):** >=70% of participants correctly identify the parry telegraph **without verbal instruction** | >=3 external testers needed for the number to be meaningful | New players only (no prior briefing) |
| PROTO-2 | **Frame-time baseline:** 50 / 100 / 200 enemies in a **player build** (record Mono/IL2CPP) on min-spec GTX 1650 / Ryzen 5 3600 / 16GB; record frame ms, enemy-tick cost if instrumented, draw calls vs 1,100 early-warning / 1,500 cap | 1 measurement pass per count (not a player session) | N/A (hardware) |

**Honest sample-size notes (solo dev):**
- M1 "min sessions" = **at least 1 developer session** (cheap, catches obvious breakage) **plus aim for 2-3 external testers**. The developer session alone cannot answer AC-13 (the developer already knows the telegraph) or any "fair/overwhelm" question.
- **A single-tester result is directional only.** Record it as such; do not treat it as sign-off on any M1 exit criterion.
- AC-13 arithmetic: with 3 testers, >=70% effectively requires 3/3 (2/3 = 67%); with 2 testers, 2/2. With 1 tester AC-13 cannot be evaluated. Say so in the report instead of rounding up.
- Frame-time numbers: if min-spec hardware is unavailable (sprint risk table), record dev-PC numbers and flag them **non-binding** for the 200-enemy budget decision (enemy tick <=4 ms, Animator+skinning <=3.0 ms, draws <=1,100). Greybox capsules without skinning will understate real cost: the baseline is a floor, not a pass.
- Not in scope for this sprint's playtest: dodge-vs-parry question (Dodge deferred to M2); the CD criterion "most players parry rather than dodge" cannot be tested in M1.

**Sign-off requirement**: Playtest notes must be written to
`production/session-logs/playtest-sprint-1-proto-2.md` (via `/playtest-report`) and reviewed by the
designer (user, acting as creative/game-design lead) before PROTO-2 can be marked COMPLETE. The report must give, per goal above, an answer (yes / no / unclear), the sample size, and which GDDs need updates (feeds the DoD item "prototype findings -> GDDs" and Sprint 2 Core-layer story creation).

## Definition of Done — This Sprint

A story is DONE when ALL of the following are true:

- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified — via automated test result OR documented
      manual evidence (screenshot, video, or playtest notes with sign-off)
- [ ] Test file exists at the specified path for all Logic and Integration stories
- [ ] Manual evidence document exists for all Visual/Feel and UI stories
- [ ] Smoke check passes (run `/smoke-check sprint` before QA hand-off)
- [ ] No regressions introduced
- [ ] Code reviewed (via `/code-review` or documented peer review)
- [ ] Story file updated to `Status: Complete` (via `/story-done`)

Sprint-1 notes on applying this DoD (solo-dev lightweight form; BLOCKING Logic/Integration gate unchanged):
- Logic/Integration stories (BCF-002/003/004/005, OP-001..004, IM-001..006, GD-003/004): test file at the path in the Test Summary **must exist and pass** before `/story-done`. No exceptions; nothing marked skipped/ignored to get CI green.
- BCF-001 (Config/Data): smoke doc + green CI run; sanity test exists.
- PROTO-1: exempt from tests/code review; DONE = playable player build handed to PROTO-2. PROTO-2: DONE = playtest report written to the path above and reviewed.
- Stories that cannot be completed because of undecided inputs (GD-003, GD-004, see gaps) stay in backlog; do not weaken their tests to close them.
- QA sign-off at sprint close: single checklist form (`/team-qa sprint`) listing each story's evidence path, open S1/S2 bugs (must be zero), and PROTO-2 verdict.
